Geochemical controls on the fate and mobility of coal combustion product-derived elements in a dolomitic aquifer
Synthetic tools to redirect the ubiquitin E3 ligase activity of a plant-specific N-recognin
articles.abstract: Abstract The Arg/N-degron pathway regulates important agronomic traits. In plants, the PROTEOLYSIS 1 (PRT1) protein binds to aromatic amino-terminal residues and recruits ubiquitin (Ub) conjugating enzymes to ubiquitinate substrate proteins. Here, we demonstrate that PRT1 recruits the UBC35-UEV1A complex via RING1 of PRT1. This stimulates UBC35 to produce K63-linked Ub chains. To afford chemical control over Ub signalling, we construct a synthetic substrate of PRT1 with an N-terminal calmodulin-binding peptide (CBP). The addition of the CBP sequence to the substrate creates an off switch for PRT1-dependent ubiquitination that is regulated by calcium and calmodulin. Finally, we produce a set of nanobodies that are recognised by PRT1 and induce the ubiquitination of a reporter protein. Altogether, we introduce and biochemically validate several tools to both redirect and chemically control the Arg/N-degron pathway.

articles.title: Weakened association between sequential phenological events corresponds to interphase extension
Sequential protonation and deprotonation reactions govern alternating access in a Major Facilitator Superfamily proton/multidrug antiporter
articles.abstract: Abstract Drug/proton antiporters of the Major Facilitator Superfamily are key drivers of antimicrobial resistance. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying proton-coupled drug efflux are inherently complex and remain unresolved. Here, we dissect the timing and mechanism of proton coupling in the multidrug transporter LmrP, a prototypical exporter of clinically relevant antibiotics and toxins. By directly tracking chamber opening in the native plasma membrane, we capture functionally relevant conformational transitions within a lipid environment and map them onto the catalytic carboxylates that govern transport. Our results suggest that earlier DEER distance measurements in detergent solution captured a restricted subset of conformational states, which our pH 8.0 data extend and place into a broader framework. Complementary pH 5.0 measurements reveal additional mechanistic features and, together, these datasets define the transport cycle in a membrane-embedded context. Supported by molecular dynamics simulations, the results reveal a coordinated, transport cycle-dependent mechanism in which paired catalytic carboxylates act sequentially in substrate binding, proton relay, gate control, and transporter resetting.

articles.title: Recruitment of TEX15 by HUSH2 drives repression of multicopy gene families in fertility regulation
Enzymes can activate and mobilize dense biomolecular condensates across scales
CO2 hydrogenation across the pressure gap over Ag/ZnO:Al2O3 catalysts
articles.abstract: Abstract The hydrogenation of carbon dioxide to value-added chemicals is a major challenge. Metal-oxide interfaces and surface structures play fundamental roles and govern the selectivity of this reaction; thus, catalysts must be investigated under relevant reaction conditions to identify structure-activity relationships and engineer more efficient materials. This work aims to elucidate mechanisms of carbon dioxide hydrogenation to methanol and side products by using operando characterization techniques within a pressure range of 1 mbar up to 15 bar. Bifunctional Ag/ZnO and Ag/ZnO:Al 2 O 3 catalysts are studied using multiple spectroscopic techniques combined with online product analysis. During catalyst activation in hydrogen, several restructuring processes of the catalyst occur at different pressures. Under carbon dioxide hydrogenation reaction conditions carbonate, formate and CH x surface intermediates show strong pressure-dependent abundances. Combining thermodynamics with in situ and operando investigations of pressure-dependent structures and intermediates allows assessing carbon dioxide hydrogenation through the pressure gap.

articles.title: Author Correction: Inactivated vaccine-elicited potent antibodies can broadly neutralize SARS-CoV-2 circulating variants
Process-dependent shifts in conspecific negative density dependence during boreal forest succession
articles.abstract: Abstract Conspecific negative density dependence (CNDD)—the stronger negative effects of conspecific than heterospecific neighbours on plant demographic performance—is a key process proposed to stabilize forest diversity, yet how it changes during succession remains poorly understood. Using a 25-year spatially explicit dataset from 148 post-fire plots in boreal forests, we show that species richness increases with stand age and that CNDD varies in process- and abundance-dependent ways across recruitment, survival, and growth. Plot-level CNDD shows no significant change with stand age in recruitment or survival, but mean relative effects are generally stronger for recruitment, and CNDD shifts from destabilizing to stabilizing for growth as stands mature. Species-level CNDD is strongly associated with species abundance, with rare species consistently experiencing stronger CNDD in recruitment and growth, whereas common species tend toward neutral or destabilizing effects. For survival, by contrast, CNDD is stronger in common than in rare species. These abundance-related differences remain broadly consistent across stand development, except in recruitment, where CNDD intensifies in rare species but remains consistently weak or near-neutral in common species. This shifting balance of density-dependent pressures highlights succession-driven trade-offs as central to species coexistence and increases in diversity in disturbance-driven forests.

articles.title: Interfacial reinforcement relieves mechanical mismatch for stable perovskite photovoltaics
One Health genomic surveillance identifies potential genetic links of antimicrobial-resistant foodborne pathogens across sectors
Video-rate volumetric chemical imaging via mid-infrared photothermal optical diffraction tomography
articles.abstract: Abstract Label-free vibrational microscopy provides chemically specific access to cellular structures, yet quantitative volumetric imaging of intracellular dynamics remains challenging on subsecond timescales. Here, we demonstrate video-rate mid-infrared photothermal optical diffraction tomography (MIP-ODT) by combining high photothermal sensitivity with rapid angular scanning. The system achieves 19.2 volumes per second, nearly 400 times faster than previous MIP tomography implementations, with a signal-to-noise ratio exceeding 70 and no temporal averaging. We track lipid droplets in living cells and quantify anomalous diffusion from three-dimensional trajectories, revealing heterogeneous intracellular transport behaviors obscured in two-dimensional measurements. Rapid mid-infrared wavenumber sweeping further enables broadband multi-wavenumber volumetric chemical imaging across a 300 cm⁻¹ spectral window within 1 s. These results establish MIP-ODT as a platform for high-speed, label-free volumetric chemical imaging of single cells and quantitative investigation of dynamic intracellular organization.

articles.title: A multilamellar organelle for chemosymbiosis in an aplacophoran mollusc adapted to anoxic cold seep sediment
Spatial patterning of hierarchical lamellar-cellular structured hydrogels for programmable deformation-coupled information encryption
Ligand hardness as a key feature differentiating base- versus noble-metal mechanisms of nickel-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura cross-couplings
articles.abstract: Abstract Nickel-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions that engage alkyl electrophiles provide potential routes for synthesis of molecules with high F sp3 . However, development of these reactions remains a challenge since the impact of ligand identity on competing mechanistic pathways is not yet well understood. To address this knowledge gap, we establish structure-reactivity trends across >550 Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reactions with known mechanistic pathways. We evaluate reaction outcome by ligand features including heteroatom identity, hybridization, bite angle, geometry, and buried volume. The most important determinant of reactivity is heteroatom identity: nitrogen-based ligands support open-shell reactions while phosphorus-based ligands support closed-shell reactions. Here we report that experimental and calculated reduction potentials and charge density analysis correlate with catalytic activity and propose a rationale for these observations based on hard-soft acid-base theory.

articles.title: A combinatorial genetics approach reveals limits to redundancy within Plasmodium falciparum invasion ligand families
articles.abstract: Abstract To maintain infection in the human bloodstream, Plasmodium falciparum parasites undergo repeated cycles of invasion of and multiplication inside red blood cells (RBCs). Two protein families, the Erythrocyte binding-like (EBA) and Reticulocyte binding-like (Rh) proteins, are known to play a key role in invasion, mediating early stages of attachment of the P. falciparum merozoite to the host RBC. There is a degree of redundancy within these families, such that disrupting the function of individual EBA/Rh proteins in vitro is not sufficient to prevent invasion. By employing a novel approach to disrupt multiple EBA and Rh genes in combination, we systematically assess functional interdependency across these families for the first time. This analysis, and further characterisation of mutant parasites, reveals that disruption of some pairs of EBA/Rh ligands significantly impacts P. falciparum invasion, whereas others do not. Disruption of PfEBA175 in combination with either PfRh2b or PfRh4 significantly reduces parasite multiplication in vitro, indicating that the remaining EBA/Rh proteins cannot fully compensate for the absence of these three key invasion ligands. PfEBA175, PfRh2b and PfRh4 may therefore represent a critical nexus of the parasite invasion machinery, and combinatorial approaches that target these specific ligands could be a beneficial therapeutic approach.

articles.title: Genomic surveillance meets clinical practice: rule-based individualized treatment prediction for gonorrhoea using SensiTyper
articles.abstract: Abstract Extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains threaten the current empirical gonorrhoea treatment. We designed and analytically validated SensiTyper, a rule-based framework that predicts antimicrobial susceptibility from whole-genome sequencing data and generates susceptibility-guided individualized treatment recommendations. SensiTyper was applied to 13,701 gonococcal genomes from 68 countries in 1928-2024, including cultured isolates and clinical molecular samples, and benchmarked predictions against previous genomic and phenotypic data. Susceptibility predictions for ceftriaxone, ciprofloxacin, spectinomycin, and zoliflodacin had 98.9-100% sensitivity and specificity. Azithromycin susceptibility predictions had 92.5% sensitivity and 97.1% specificity, and gepotidacin susceptibility prediction 100% sensitivity, but 0% specificity, illustrating that low-level phenotypic gepotidacin resistance is not caused by the only known resistance determinants (GyrA A92T plus ParC D86N). The SensiTreat module integrates antimicrobial susceptibility profiles into sequential treatment logic, providing susceptibility-guided individualized treatment recommendations while also enabling alternative stewardship strategies prioritizing, e.g., ciprofloxacin. SensiTyper flags XDR isolates for expert follow-up, test-of-cure and comprehensive contact tracing. In conclusion, SensiTyper is a robust and adaptable approach for gonococcal antimicrobial susceptibility prediction, individualized gonorrhoea treatment and antimicrobial stewardship.

articles.title: Precise modular engineering of neutral organometallic rectangles from binuclear palladacycles via hierarchical assembly strategy
articles.abstract: Abstract Metallosupramolecular assembly provides a powerful strategy for the precise construction of well-defined architectures with diverse topologies and functionalities. However, the construction of neutral organometallic architectures supported by robust metal-carbon bonds remains underdeveloped, largely because kinetic persistence limits the reversible structural correction required for conventional self-assembly. Herein, we employ binuclear palladacycles as intrinsically neutral and geometrically preorganized building blocks and develop a hierarchical assembly strategy that temporally separates geometric programming, scaffold editing, and topology locking. Through a polymerization-cleavage-assembly process, cyclopalladated polymers are converted into discrete binuclear precursors while retaining their programmed geometrical information. Subsequent trans-effect-directed N -heterocyclic carbene ligation affords a series of size-tunable, kinetically robust, and neutral organometallic rectangles. The resulting architectures are fully characterized by spectroscopic methods and single crystal X-ray diffraction analyses. Moreover, single crystal X-ray diffraction identifies guest-mediated breathing-like geometric deformations in the solid state, driven by exo-wall π-π stacking and charge-transfer interactions with both electron-rich and electron-deficient planar guests. This work establishes a hierarchical construction principle for accessing discrete neutral organometallic architectures by separating geometric programming from the final locking of the topology through strong bond formation, while demonstrating that local geometric adaptation can occur without disrupting the framework connectivity established by Pd-C bonds.

articles.title: Genome-scale eCLIP mapping of SARS-CoV-2 RNA interactions with NSP8, NSP12, and N reveals regulatory sites
articles.abstract: Abstract The global impact of the COVID-19 pandemic highlights the need for a deeper understanding of SARS-CoV-2 replication. Although the essential roles of the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (NSP12), primase (NSP8), and nucleocapsid (N) proteins are established, their contact points with the full-length viral RNA genome during active infection require further characterization. Here, we used enhanced crosslinking and immunoprecipitation (eCLIP) to map direct interactions of NSP8, NSP12, and N across the SARS-CoV-2 genome during live virus infection at early and late stages of replication. We mapped NSP8 and NSP12 binding to the 5′ and 3′ ends of positive- and negative-sense RNA, consistent with their roles in viral replication, transcription, and translation. We also observed an NSP12 binding site within the conserved Y1 domain of NSP3 that modulates RNA and protein abundance. In addition, N binds the 5′ untranslated region (UTR), supporting a role in translational regulation early in infection, and associates with the frameshift element, where it modulates ribosomal frameshifting. Together, these findings map SARS-CoV-2 RNA–protein interactions across the viral genome and delineate specific regulatory regions for potential antiviral intervention.

articles.title: Minimally invasive topological light manipulation with lensless fiber endomicroscope
B7-H4‒directed antibody-drug conjugate AZD8205 (puxitatug samrotecan) in patients with advanced/metastatic solid tumors: the Phase 1/2a (BLUESTAR), first-in-human study

Fog
Intensity and Droplet Size-Resolved Aqueous Secondary
Organic Aerosol (aqSOA) Formation in Polluted Winter Fog: New Insights
from a Combined Observational and Modeling Study
articles.abstract: Abstract Fog is a chemically active aqueous medium in which dissolved organic gases and particles are converted into highly oxidized aqueous secondary organic aerosol (aqSOA). Its magnitude is difficult to constrain, and most published estimates rely on models. We analyzed size-resolved fogwater collected over two winters at Kanpur, India, by offline high-resolution aerosol mass spectrometry and apportioned by positive matrix factorization (PMF). Three highly oxidized factors (O/C 0.95–1.19) were summed as an aqSOA proxy. Combining this proxy with colocated liquid water content and water-soluble organic carbon yielded 3.1–8.4 μg m–3 aqSOA across seven events. The droplet aqSOA accounts for a median of about 7% of ambient SOA and 5% of ambient OA, reaching 13% of SOA in the densest fogs. Fine droplets carried the largest aqSOA share (43–84%), driven by higher concentrations of dissolved Fe and Cu and longer residence times. Ambient OA was less oxidized during dense than light fog (O/C 0.52 versus 0.61). Returning aqSOA after dissipation gave direct-radiative-effect increments of −0.048 W m–2 (dense) and −0.032 W m–2 (light). These size- and intensity-resolved observational constraints quantify fog–aerosol interactions and their air quality consequences in a heavily polluted region.

articles.title:
Dual-Isotope Tracing
Reveals Substantial Postanthesis
Foliar and Panicle Contributions to Grain Cadmium Accumulation in
Hydroponically Grown Rice
articles.abstract: Abstract Cadmium (Cd) accumulation in rice grains occurs through multiple exposure pathways, yet the relative contributions and associated transport mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we applied dual stable isotope labeling (112Cd/113Cd) in hydroponically grown rice under controlled conditions, with root exposure through nutrient solution as well as foliar and panicle exposure through direct solution spraying. Source apportionment was complemented by sap analysis and triple-quadrupole LA-ICP-MS imaging to examine vascular transport and allocation in the first node under the panicle (node I). Direct Cd contact with aboveground tissues inhibited growth more strongly than root exposure, inducing antioxidant responses and stomatal limitation. Isotopic mass balance revealed that under controlled hydroponic root/foliar exposure, postanthesis Cd inputs contributed 80% and 90% of grain Cd, respectively. Under triple exposure, grain Cd averaged 0.558 mg kg–1, comprising 40% foliar, 24% panicle, and 36% root contributions, demonstrating that aboveground contributions were comparable to root contributions. Transport routes diverged: root uptake elevated xylem sap Cd, whereas foliar-derived Cd showed phloem-associated localization in node I and enrichment in phloem exudates. These results highlight the role of aboveground sources in grain Cd accumulation and suggest that risk assessment in deposition-affected areas should consider both root and aboveground Cd inputs, especially during reproduction.

articles.title:
Unraveling the Differentiated
Roles of Reactive Chlorine
in Regulating Atmospheric Oxidation and Secondary Formation
articles.abstract: Abstract Reactive chlorine species significantly perturb atmospheric oxidation, yet systematic observations of multiple chlorine species and comprehensive assessments of their distinct photochemical roles remain limited. Here, we present concurrent field measurements of four reactive chlorine species (ClNO2, Cl2, HOCl, and NCl3) in a coastal urban atmosphere. Cl2 photolysis dominated Cl• production (40.2%), whereas HOCl photolysis served as a dual source of Cl• and OH•, a mechanism previously overlooked, and most effectively elevated ROx• levels. Temporally, ClNO2 photolysis enhanced early morning oxidation, Cl2 prevailed around noon, and HOCl dominated the afternoon radical budgets, while NCl3 photolysis contributed minimally throughout the diurnal cycle. Incorporating chlorine-induced volatile organic compounds (VOC) consumption in the box model amplified O3 and PAN production by up to 43.4 and 43.8%, respectively, without altering the VOC-limited regime. Our findings underscored that regulating coastal atmospheric oxidation required a species-specific, time-resolved treatment of chlorine chemistry, with direct implications for air quality management.

articles.title:
Small
Modular Electrochemical
Containers for Decarbonization
of AI Data Centers
articles.abstract: Abstract The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is increasing data-center electricity demand and reinforcing the near-term role of fossil-fuel power generation. Decarbonizing this infrastructure requires carbon capture systems that are efficient, compact, modular, and compatible with space-constrained data centers. Here, we evaluate Small Modular Electrochemical Containers (SMECs) as a deployment-oriented application of a two-stage, membraneless electrochemically mediated amine regeneration (EMAR) process. The design integrates CO2 absorption and electrochemical desorption within one gas-diffusion-electrode cell, eliminating absorber columns and ion-exchange membranes. Single-cell experiments were conducted under simulated natural-gas and coal-derived flue gas. Polarization mapping identified optimized operating conditions, which were then used in a 300-cycle, 50-h accelerated stability test with periodic polarity switching. The cell maintained repeatable voltage and CO2 absorption/desorption profiles, with absorption and desorption efficiencies of ∼90% under optimized conditions. The energetics ranged from 50–85 kJe/molCO2, and GC/IC analyses showed no detectable gaseous or liquid side products. The paper further includes theoretical modeling of SOx and NOx effects on the absorbent. In a case study for a 360 MW data-center power plant, the TEA showed that fewer than 20 SMEC units could achieve near-complete decarbonization, increasing the levelized electricity cost from about \$58/MWh to \$74/MWh.

articles.title:
The End of Uniformity:
Spatial, Climatic, and Toxicological
Redefinitions of Air Quality
Proteomic Profiling for In Situ Exposure in a Sentinel Freshwater Species to Describe the Crustacean Reproductive Effects of Aquatic Contamination
articles.abstract: Abstract Complex mixtures of contaminants can affect aquatic organisms through diverse modes of action, making extrapolations of laboratory findings to field conditions complex. Here, we show that proteomics combined with active biomonitoring may inform about reprotoxic effects in the sentinel species Gammarus fossarum. Proteomic responses provide information on the diversity of underlying mechanisms and may serve as a sensitive early warning signal of reprotoxicity. Females were exposed in situ in 18 French surveillance sites and analyzed for reproductive end points and proteomic levels in the caeca and the ovaries. This study aimed to assess links between reproductive impairment and molecular responses, using the complementary information provided by both tissues. Protein coexpression analysis identified protein clusters associated with organ functions, reproductive impairments, or field exposure. Several modules were significantly associated with field condition or females’ physiological integrity. Interestingly, we identified a large diversity of biological pathways modulated in impacted females exposed to reprotoxic sites, with reproduction-related proteins as potential early biomarkers of reprotoxicity. These results highlight the relevance of considering field conditions and individual physiology within the eco-exposome framework and demonstrate the value of integrating omics and active biomonitoring to uncover diverse molecular signature behind field-induced reprotoxicity in this sentinel species.

articles.title:
Industrial Solid
Wastes Recycling from Steel and Power
Sectors Delivers Climate and Net Societal Benefits
articles.abstract: Abstract Sectoral decarbonization can substantially reshape the quantity and composition of industrial solid waste and its associated resource recovery potential, yet how these changes evolve along decarbonization pathways remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a sectoral transition framework linking future waste generation, recycling technologies, life cycle environmental impacts, and societal benefits. We focus on the steel and power sectors, which represent major industrial solid waste sources and distinct decarbonization pathways across six major producing regions from 2025 to 2050. By 2050, steel sector wastes remain at 0.61–0.78 Gt, whereas power sector wastes decline from 1.11 Gt in 2025 to 0.17–0.50 Gt. Under four scenarios, cumulative mitigation ranges from 25.68 to 53.39 Gt CO2-eq, with discounted net societal benefits of USD 11.24–23.81 trillion. Steel sector benefits are sensitive to recycling technology shares, whereas power sector benefits are more strongly shaped by transition-driven changes in the waste generation and composition. These findings highlight the importance of integrating evolving waste flows and technology choices into long-term decarbonization and circular economy strategies.

articles.title:
Lipophilic
Redox
Mediators Reprogram Intracellular
Electron Flow to Promote Arsenic Methylation in Soil Fermentative
Bacteria
articles.abstract: Abstract Anaerobic arsenic (As) methylation by fermentative microorganisms, particularly Clostridium-related populations, controls As speciation, mobility, and volatilization in flooded paddy soils, yet the mechanisms promoting this process remain poorly understood. Here, we reveal that phenazine- and phenoxazine-like redox mediators can enhance anaerobic As methylation via reshaping the intracellular electron allocation in a representative As-methylating fermentative bacterium. We integrated As speciation analysis, metabolite profiling, proteomics, and metabolic-flux modeling to determine how resazurin, as a represenative lipophilic redox mediator, reshapes fermentative metabolism and methylated As (MeAs) formation. The membrane-permeable redox mediator resazurin increased the apparent rate constant of MeAs formation by up to fourfold relative to the hydrophilic mediator anthraquinone-2,6-disulfonic acid (AQDS). Unlike AQDS, resazurin enhanced dimethylarsine formation while establishing a more reducing intracellular environment by diverting electrons from hydrogen evolution, indicating altered intracellular electron disposal. At the proteomic level, resazurin induced coordinated increases in As(III) methyltransferase (ArsM) and proteins involved in S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) biosynthesis, representing the primary molecular responses associated with enhanced As methylation. Proteins involved in amino-acid-fueled energy conservation and redox homeostasis were also enriched, potentially creating favorable cellular conditions for SAM-dependent As methylation. In a paddy-soil-derived fermentative consortium, resazurin likewise enhanced MeAs production and increased transcript levels of Clostridium-associated arsM and the SAM synthetase gene (metK). These findings identify lipophilicity-dependent, redox-compound-mediated intracellular electron flow reprogramming as a previously underappreciated control on anaerobic As methylation and provide a mechanistic basis for predicting MeAs formation in flooded soil environments.

articles.title:
A
Framework for Time-Explicit Life Cycle Optimization
articles.abstract: Abstract Life cycle optimization (LCO) selects optimal processes and supply chains from a set of alternatives given environmental constraints and objectives, supporting the design of sustainable systems and their transitions. However, current approaches rely on static assumptions, overlooking two interacting temporal dimensions: temporal distribution (flows are spread over time) and temporal evolution (processes and supply chains change over time). Because distribution and evolution jointly dictate the magnitude of a flow at a given time, both must be considered simultaneously to accurately optimize against cumulative environmental impacts and time-specific environmental constraints. We present a framework for time-explicit LCO that captures these interdependencies to determine optimal transition pathways. The framework tracks flow timing relative to process installation and dynamically determines flow magnitudes from time-specific process parameters and background supply chains. A case study on integrated methanol and pig iron production demonstrates how time-explicit LCO enables optimization against time-resolved environmental impacts and constraints, revealing mitigation strategies inaccessible to static approaches: prioritizing early high-efficiency technology installation to idle older processes as operational savings outweigh embodied impacts of stranded assets, and avoiding transient resource bottlenecks through diversification. To facilitate widespread application, we provide the open-source Python package optimex, enabling practitioners to design transition pathways that rigorously respect environmental limits.

articles.title:
Pesky Metals: Historical
Perspective, Advances, and
Challenges for Remediation of Problematic Metal Contaminants
articles.abstract: Abstract Persistent and problematic toxic metal and metalloid pollutants (in particular, As, Hg, Pb, Cd, and Cr) have long been challenging and expensive remediation targets in contaminated surface and subsurface environments. Since the advent of environmental regulations and cleanup in the late 20th century, much progress has been made to address sites of legacy metal pollution and limit new contamination. Despite this, metal pollution remains a global problem, particularly in soils and sediments, with many large legacy sites inadequately remediated, metal contamination widespread in developed and developing nations, and new pollution occurring from informal and often illegal extraction and recycling processes. In this perspective, we highlight advances and challenges in science and technology, and key economic and social factors, that have influenced remediation of these “pesky” metals over the last ∼50 years. Through this lens, we consider emerging challenges and opportunities associated with legacy and critical metals, climate resilience, and sustainability.

articles.title: Unregulated Disinfection Byproducts from de facto Water Reuse: Molecular Evidence for EfOM-Induced Redirection of Chlorination Pathways
articles.abstract: Abstract Unplanned potable reuse introduces effluent-derived organic matter (EfOM) into drinking water sources. While conventional coagulation partially removes EfOM, the residual fraction undergoes chlorination and may form toxic disinfection byproducts (DBPs) that escape current monitoring. However, the molecular mechanisms by which EfOM alters DBP formation pathways remain poorly understood. Here, we combine ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrometry with reaction network analysis to reveal that EfOM significantly redirects chlorine pathways. Compared to EfOM-free surface water, the presence of 20% EfOM decreases direct halogenation pathways (addition and substitution) from 4.2% to 1.8% of total transformation events. This shift occurs because EfOM introduces reduced, high-molecular-weight, heteroatom-rich molecules that cannot be directly halogenated; they require HOCl-driven oxidative fragmentation to generate halogenation-susceptible intermediates. Consequently, chlorinated finished water accumulates sulfur-containing DBPs (CHOS compounds, with relative intensity increasing from 35% to 60%) and complex “orphan” DBPs lacking identifiable precursors (with molecular features linked to elevated toxicity). These findings highlight an urgent need to update DBP monitoring frameworks to include unregulated sulfur-containing and orphan byproducts in de facto reuse scenarios.

articles.title:
Unveiling
Seven-Decade Disparities of Methane Emissions
across China
articles.abstract: Abstract China’s century-long economic transition generated substantial methane emissions, yet the trajectory and factors of this evolution remain poorly quantified. A systematic understanding is essential for reconciling China’s economic growth with emission mitigation targets and for informing Global South nations. Using a bottom-up estimate of subnational methane emissions (1949–2022), we uncover a fundamental shift from agriculture-dominated to industry-dominated methane emissions in China. Nationwide emissions peaked in 2012, declining 3.8% by 2022, yet provincial disparities widened by 48%. While superficially reflecting heterogeneous fossil fuel use, these disparities are attributable to a shift in explanatory dominance from purely economic to dual economic-policy factors, particularly carbon policies. The long-term stability in agricultural sectors reflects nationwide efforts to food security, which maintains a baseline level of production across provinces. Recent regional decoupling masks the disproportion between emissions and economic gains. Western provinces (e.g., Shanxi, Ningxia, Guizhou) continue to exhibit high-emission but low-return economic profiles. The average of their methane emissions per GDP was 4.8 times that of eastern regions in 2022, with extremes reaching 150-fold differences. For equitable mitigation, future focus should shift from “who emits” to “why emits”, establishing a scientific basis for fair compensation between resource-dependent and resource-consuming regions.

articles.title:
Subsoil
versus Topsoil Straw Addition Shifts Microbial
Carbon Allocation for Enhanced Carbon Sequestration and Emission Mitigation
articles.abstract: Abstract Subsoils (>20 cm) represent an underutilized sink for soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration because C inputs in subsoil are typically limited. To clarify how organic inputs regulate subsoil SOC accrual and C emissions in rice paddies, we combined a 2-year field experiment with 13C-labeled straw incubation and validated the results with a global meta-analysis. Results showed that compared with no addition and topsoil straw addition, subsoil straw addition increased SOC stocks by 10.5% and 2.2%, respectively, primarily via enhanced mineral-associated organic C (MAOC) formation at 0–30 cm. The 270-day incubation revealed that subsoil addition accelerated microbial conversion of straw C into amino sugars, evidenced by 13C-phospholipid fatty acids, promoting MAOC formation. Relative to topsoil addition, subsoil addition reduced CH4 emissions by 15.3%, driven by improved root growth and enhanced CH4 oxidation, and decreased CO2 emissions by lowering topsoil C availability and peroxidase activity. Meta-analysis confirmed that C emissions decrease progressively with increasing incorporation depth, and machine-learning models indicate that deeper incorporation (>20 cm) mitigates global C emissions by half under future climate change. Overall, compared with topsoil addition, subsoil addition represents a win–win strategy that simultaneously enhances SOC sequestration and reduces C emissions, with potential applicability beyond paddy systems.

articles.title:
Mapping the Carbon
Footprint of Organic Chemicals
in Commerce
articles.abstract: Abstract The chemical industry is a major contributor to global CO2 emissions, accounting for ∼10% of total greenhouse gases, underscoring the need for a sustainability transition. However, public carbon footprint data exists for only hundreds of the more than 100,000 chemicals in commerce, limiting effective action. To address this, we collect high-quality primary chemical carbon footprint data and refine a machine learning model to estimate the carbon footprint of 94,697 chemicals in commerce across 26 national and regional chemical inventories. Our analysis reveals clear molecular structure–carbon footprint relationships that may guide future molecular design: carbon footprints are strongly linked to molecular frameworks, the number of ring structures, and types of heteroatoms. Newly commercialized chemicals tend to have higher carbon footprints than older chemicals, emphasizing the urgent need to embed “sustainable-by-design” principles into chemical innovation from the outset. This study provides a database of chemical carbon footprints and actionable insights for the sustainable design and use of chemicals, supporting the environmental decision-making of chemical producers, consumers, and policymakers.

articles.title:
The
Subclinical Cardiovascular Effects of Nonoptimum
Ambient Temperature: A Longitudinal Study in 15 Chinese Cities
articles.abstract: Abstract Short-term ambient temperature is linked to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, but subclinical responses remain unclear. Using repeated health examinations from 247,641 adults in 15 Chinese cities (2013–2020), we assessed 20 cardiovascular indicators with linear mixed-effects and distributed lag nonlinear models. The indicator-specific sample sizes ranged from 1119 to 219,090 participants. Exposure–response relationships were near-linear or inversely J-shaped for ten indicators, U-shaped or inverted U-shaped for seven, and atypical or unclear for three. Low temperature was associated with 18 indicators, peaking at lags 0–5 days, whereas high temperature was associated with seven, peaking at lags 0–6 days. Relative to the reference temperatures, extremely low-temperature exposure (P1, −9 °C) was associated with cumulative increases over lag days 0–10 of 6.52%–13.99% in blood pressure, 4.63%–46.23% in inflammatory markers, 5.11%–10.48% in cardiac-associated enzymes, and 6.29% in homocysteine, as well as cumulative changes ranging from −2.68% to 5.36% in hemorheological parameters and from −4.96% to 12.05% in lipid-related indicators. Extremely high-temperature exposure (P99, 32 °C) was associated with cumulative changes ranging from −1.47% to 4.84% in hemorheological parameters and increases of 1.62%–1.91% in lipid indicators and 1.32%–15.13% in cardiac-associated enzymes. These findings provide multicenter evidence that nonoptimum temperature is associated with early cardiovascular alterations.

articles.title:
Longitudinal
Multiomics Reveals Core Microbiome Disruption
and Potential Keystone-Associated Recovery Following Pesticide Exposure
articles.abstract: Abstract Pesticides have become indispensable in modern agriculture, serving as a primary tool to minimize crop loss amid increasing human population pressures. While the negative effects of pesticides on the soil microbiome have been reported, the temporal dynamics of soil microorganisms under pesticide use remain underexplored. Specifically, limited knowledge exists regarding how the soil microbiome responds to pesticides before and after the manufacturer-labeled ‘safe period’ of 21 days after application. We conducted a longitudinal microcosm study to investigate the temporal impacts of herbicide, fungicide, and insecticide on soil microbial diversity, composition, network complexity, and functional pathways across five time points. Our results show that soil microbial communities are negatively impacted by pesticide applications, but there is a trend of recovery after 21 days. We found a significant impact of the temporal persistence of pesticides on both bacterial and fungal community composition, with a stronger effect on fungi. Network analysis revealed that core microbiome networks were negatively impacted by pesticide applications, with the core microbial nodes, raw associations, and modularity declining in pesticide-treated soils, and this negative effect was particularly strong for pyrethroid insecticides. We identified several differentially abundant taxa, including Xanthobacteraceae and Vicinamibacteriales among bacteria, and Mortierella, Mytilinidales among fungi, which could serve as useful biomarkers for pesticide-affected soils. Results from microbial co-occurrence network analysis revealed that one ASV assigned to the Methyloligellaceae family consistently emerged as a keystone taxon in pesticide-treated soils. Using genome-resolved metagenomics, we assembled the genomes (MAGs) of Methyloligellaceae members and found these taxa harbor putative genes associated with pesticide degradation and antimicrobial resistance, suggesting their possible role in community recovery. Given the remarkably dynamic nature of soil microbial communities, our findings bridge an important knowledge gap regarding the short-term dynamics of microbial structures and functional pathways in response to major pesticides.

articles.title:
Unraveling
the Bound-Water
Removal Mystery: Preoxidation
Enhances Sludge Dewatering via Cell Permeabilization and Transformation
of Intracellular Polymeric Substances to Extracellular Polymeric Substances
articles.abstract: Abstract The effect of oxidation degree on sludge dewaterability during oxone-induced preoxidation was investigated. The optimal oxone concentration increased free cells and membrane permeabilization while limiting cell lysis, releasing bound water, and producing a drier sludge cake without reducing the filtrate volume. Dewaterability enhancement was mainly driven by the shift of low-molecular-weight proteins and polysaccharides (<20 kDa) from intracellular polymeric substances (IPS) to extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), along with selective degradation of hydrophilic glucose and peptidoglycan in EPS. Organic matter transferred to the outer EPS layer was mainly derived from the cellular constituents of Gram-negative bacteria in sludge. Importantly, IPS was found to exert a distinct and non-negligible influence on sludge dewatering with its oxidative response fundamentally differing from that of EPS. As the oxidation intensity increased, the ratio of protein to polysaccharide rose in loosely bound EPS but declined in IPS, whereas carboxyl and lactone groups decreased in both soluble and loosely bound EPS fractions, while carboxyl groups concurrently increased within IPS. IPS contained more hydrophobic components than did EPS at all oxone concentrations. Excessive oxidation induced cell disruption and hydrophilic debris, impairing sludge dewaterability. Cell membrane permeabilization, rather than cell lysis, was the key factor affecting sludge dewaterability.

articles.title: Deriving Organism-Relevant Nanoparticle Safety Exposure Limits from In Vitro Toxicity Data
articles.abstract: Abstract Establishing human safety limits of engineered nanoparticles remains a challenge. In vitro assays have become a major toxicity data resource, driven by the demand for new approach methodologies (NAMs) that reduce animal testing. However, robust tools that bridge in vitro data with in vivo outcomes are still lacking. Here, we present an integrated computational framework using physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling to derive organism-level BMD10-based dose estimates directly from in vitro liver toxicity data. For 4 nondissolvable nanoparticles (TiO2, SiO2, Au, and graphene oxide), we curated in vitro toxicity data sets spanning 7 liver-relevant cell systems (5 human and 2 mouse) across 24 assays and estimated in vitro effect thresholds using the benchmark dose for a 10% response (BMD10). Mouse in vitro BMD10 values were then reverse-translated into predicted BMD10IVIVE values using a validated mouse PBPK model and benchmarked against available mouse-derived in vivo effect threshold (BMD10eq) data to ensure consistency. The resulting nanoparticle-specific BMD10IVIVE ranges showed qualitative concordance with animal-derived reference doses, supporting the biological plausibility of these screening-level dose estimates. We further applied the same workflow to human liver cell systems to derive human-relevant BMD10-based points of departure. This approach establishes a scalable and prospective animal-free workflow for human nanoparticle risk assessments, overcoming a critical translational gap.

articles.title:
Nanoconfinement
Decouples Calcium-Enhanced Phosphate
Capture from Calcium Phosphate Crystal Maturation
articles.abstract: Abstract Calcium phosphate (Ca–P) scaling, which is ubiquitous in nature and in water systems, has been shown to interfere with the capture of phosphate by ferric oxide-based sorbents, thereby deteriorating their decontamination performance in repeated cycles. Here, we show that a specifically designed gel-type nanocomposite, namely HFO@N201, enables Ca-enhanced phosphate sequestration while restricting Ca–P scaling via nanoconfinement. Increasing the initial Ca2+ concentration from 0 to 160 mg/L improved phosphate uptake from ∼4.5 to ∼6.2 mg/g in the first cycle. After 20 adsorption-regeneration cycles, phosphate uptake remained at ∼6.4 mg/g in the Ca-containing system, twice that of ∼3.2 mg/g in the Ca-free system. In fixed-bed tests, the presence of Ca2+ enhanced the working capacity from ∼1350 to ∼1800 bed volumes, which could be observed again in the subsequent cycle. Asynchronous release of Fe, P, and Ca during acidic elution of P-loaded HFO@N201 indicates heterogeneous and nonstoichiometric Ca-associated phosphate retention rather than formation of a mature bulk Ca–P phase. XRD, TEM, EXAFS, and Mössbauer spectroscopy further show that the retained Ca–P species remained weakly ordered and that the nanosized ferrihydrite-like Fe phase persisted during cyclic operation. Thermodynamic analysis, classical nucleation theory, and molecular dynamics simulations further support that the nanoconfinement structure of HFO@N201 (∼2 nm) creates a low-mobility hydration environment that restricts solvent exchange, ion rearrangement, and long-range ordering, thereby stabilizing Ca–P species in a weakly ordered interfacial state. Our work demonstrates nanoconfinement as a strategy to exploit Ca-enhanced phosphate capture while reducing Ca–P scaling in regenerable sorbents.
